discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris, and Flatiron Institute, New York

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that the Hubbard model becomes exactly tractable in infinite dimensions. Georges and Kotliar then turned this insight into dynamical mean-field theory, mapping a lattice of interacting electrons onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. DMFT gave the first unified, non-perturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It captures quasiparticles and Hubbard bands on equal footing, explaining the spectra of transition-metal oxides, and it resolved long-standing puzzles such as the volume collapse in plutonium and cerium. Combined with density-functional theory, DFT+DMFT is now the standard predictive first-principles framework for correlated materials, from iron-based superconductors to the Earth's core, magnets and nickelates, and it is confirmed quantitatively by photoemission and high-pressure experiments. The theory transformed correlated-electron physics from qualitative modelling into quantitative materials science, with impact across condensed matter, chemistry and geophysics.
